title: Public Key vs Private Key: Your Crypto Mailbox Explained (Beginner Guide)
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. A public key is like a mailbox anyone can send to. A private key is the key that opens it. Sources: Trezor, CoinDesk, Bitpanda, MoonPay. AI-generated voice.

scenes.head: TWO KEYS, ONE WALLET
scenes.narration: Every crypto wallet runs on two keys. One you can share, and one you must never share. Do you know which is which?

scenes.head: THE MAILBOX
scenes.narration: Your public key, or address, works like a mailbox. Anyone can drop crypto in, and sharing it is normal.

scenes.head: THE KEY TO OPEN IT
scenes.narration: Your private key is the key to that mailbox. It proves you own the funds and approves every payment you send.

scenes.head: WHO HAS THE KEY?
items: No help desk to reset it
scenes.narration: Whoever holds the private key controls the funds. There is usually no help desk to reset it, so a lost key can mean lost access.

scenes.head: HOW IT GETS STOLEN
scenes.narration: Scammers ask for keys through fake support messages and phishing sites. Never type them into a website or store them online.

scenes.head: SAFE HABITS
scenes.narration: Keep backups offline, never share your keys with anyone, and always double-check an address before you send.
